description: issue #681 (slice I2), the tooling half of the slice: with `interaction-events` active, a program that USES `input` checks clean. Both halves of a name`s registration land in this slice — the reader/checker arity entry (`packages/parser/src/signatures.ts`) and the runtime evaluator — so a program that checks clean is a program the runtime can actually execute. The tooling slice (#687) deliberately left `input` out for exactly that reason: registering a known callee with no evaluator behind it would let a program check clean and then fail at runtime. `input` is nested inside a procedure body rather than sitting at top level, so a registration that only handled a top-level occurrence cannot pass. This is a check-mode fixture: it proves static NAME VISIBILITY and arity only — the execution fixtures beside it cover the read itself.
